decisions.rationale: OLiA Adjective covers the lexical adjective POS and the ExtraBiblical original MQL declares adjv as a word.sp part-of-speech enum member, with a nonzero value in the exact TF inventory. The shared ETCBC BHSA tagset also defines adjv as adjective; pending direct original MQL code/line validation, this is a proposed category-level match.

OLiA Adverb is the generic adverb morphosyntactic class. The ExtraBiblical pinned word.sp TF inventory contains advb, while related ETCBC BHSA documentation defines that code as adverb. This is a proposed annotation-category correspondence, not a claim about every token's syntactic adjunct behavior; verify original MQL discriminant.

The ExtraBiblical original POS enum and pinned TF inventory identify art. Shared ETCBC/BHSA feature documentation glosses this POS code as article, matching OLiA Article as a determiner subtype. The annotation category is being mapped, not definiteness of any individual article; verify its actual MQL declaration.

The native ExtraBiblical TF word.sp domain includes conj and its type is defined in the original part_of_speech_t enumeration. In the shared ETCBC category vocabulary conj means conjunction. OLiA Conjunction is deliberately the generic POS, not a coordinating or subordinating subtype.

The ExtraBiblical word.sp code inrg is attested in the native TF inventory but its original MQL enumerator gives no documented particle-vs-adverb-vs-pronoun definition. Despite BHSA's interrogative particle gloss, retain native-only rather than declare an exact OLiA InterrogativeParticle equivalence solely from a shared code name.

The ExtraBiblical original MQL word.sp enum and exact pinned TF domain include intj. The closely related ETCBC BHSA part-of-speech vocabulary defines this category as interjection, corresponding to the OLiA Interjection class. This maps grammatical annotation type, not independent discourse or emotion semantics.

The ExtraBiblical original MQL enum and TF inventory include nega, but the source abbreviation by itself does not prove that every occurrence is a negative particle rather than another type of negative expression. Inherited BHSA glosses are supporting evidence only; do not assert exact OLiA NegativeParticle yet.

The ExtraBiblical word.sp category prde follows the shared ETCBC part-of-speech vocabulary for demonstrative pronouns and occurs in the pinned TF inventory. OLiA DemonstrativePronoun specifically models the pronoun class, not all demonstrative determiners; the original MQL enumeration and relationship must be checked.

The ExtraBiblical source POS enum contains prep, and the exact TF inventory counts many word.sp=prep occurrences. Shared ETCBC/BHSA documentation defines prep as preposition, matching the OLiA Preposition lexical category without inventing tokenization or prepositional phrase semantics.

The original ExtraBiblical POS inventory identifies prin, whose shared ETCBC/BHSA classification is interrogative pronoun. OLiA InterrogativePronoun is this pronoun subtype. Distinguish it from word.sp=inrg and do not infer equivalence merely because both involve questions.

The ExtraBiblical native POS inventory contains prps, associated in BHSA's related ETCBC feature vocabulary with personal pronouns. OLiA PersonalPronoun explicitly narrows to irreflexive personal pronouns; the ExtraBiblical original MQL enum does not establish irreflexivity for this category, so keep native-only.
